description: Load a list of store locations in one call — opening a chain, migrating from another system. For one shop use create_outlet. Name, street address, city, state and postal code are ALL required on new rows, exactly as in the cabinet form; ask the merchant rather than inventing an address. Country is not settable: every outlet takes the company country, and the import fails outright if the company has none. This tool does NOT match rows against what already exists — the cabinet does that in the browser, not on the server. Every row in `creates` becomes a NEW record even if an identical one is already there. To change existing records, read them with export_records and pass their ids in `updates`. Bulk-created outlets differ from ones added in the cabinet in two ways worth telling the merchant: no Stripe location is wired up (payments must be linked per outlet afterwards) and stock rows are seeded in the background, so a fresh outlet can look empty for a while. This path also does NOT check the plan allowance, so it can push the company past the number of outlets it pays for — say so before importing more than a couple. Updates only set what you pass; alias and country cannot be changed here. Rows are independent and per-row failures come back in the reply. Max 500 rows per call. BEFORE CALLING: show the merchant a preview of the first few rows, state the EXACT number of rows and which resource they hit, and get an explicit yes. There is NO undo and no dry-run — nothing here validates without writing. If you are unsure a row is right, ask; a wrong bulk import is far more expensive to repair than a question. Afterwards, tell the merchant what landed: an import done here does NOT appear in the cabinet's Recent Imports list, which only records uploads made through the wizard.

alias.description: Short label; set once and cannot be changed later

outletId.description: Existing outlet id from export_records or get_outlets
